name: rotaris-crw-windows
about: This repository's commands and places on a Windows host with a display (Git Bash shells, Node 24 the default `node`, no `xvfb-run`): the same commands as profiles/rotaris-crw.json with the Linux display wrapper removed, and duress detached without `setsid`, which Git Bash lacks. They are Git Bash commands: `timeout` is GNU coreutils' there, and Windows' pause command under PowerShell or cmd. Render with `--repo` in forward slashes (`--repo C:/dev/Rotaris-crw`): the default reads the checkout as `C:\dev\Rotaris-crw`, whose backslashes an agent's Git Bash reads as escapes. {repo} is the primary checkout; {id} is the plan id; agents read this skill from the orchestration's own detached reference worktree {repo}-wt-skillref-{id}; {node24} becomes the PATH export a host needs for Node 24, or a no-op where Node 24 is already the default; {node} becomes the Node 24 binary for a command that takes no shell prefix (the live runs: one absolute command each, since an agent's shell starts every command in the primary checkout and an allow rule matches only the command as sent). Session-specific values (trailers, extra push targets, model) come from the plan.

run.setup: pnpm install --prefer-offline && node node_modules/electron/install.js && pnpm symbols
run.quickGate: pnpm symbols && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint
run.afterMerge: pnpm install --prefer-offline (only if pnpm-lock.yaml changed) && pnpm symbols

proofs.run: timeout 1500 node apps/desktop/scripts/<name>.mjs --skip-build (no display wrapper on Windows: each launch opens real windows on the desktop; drop --skip-build only where the script's header says it takes none; docs/proofs/README.md says what each needs)

live.note: Each command names its own Node 24 binary, and the script judges the tree it sits in, whatever your directory. That tree needs the code-intelligence bundle, which the build does not make and without which a `--skip-build` launch refuses at once: run `pnpm code-intel:bundle` in it first (seconds when it is already there). The third run is the opt-in scenarios, which the default run leaves out.

runs.what: the default live run, every scenario

duress, with the window the endpoint needs (docs/proofs/live-run.md sets LIVE_RUN_DURESS_MS=7800000, and the launch's own bound is the wait plus 180 s). It outlives the Bash tool's 7,200,000 ms background cap, so it is launched DETACHED (Git Bash has no `setsid`; `nohup … & disown` outlives the shell that sent it). Send the command as written (it returns at once), then wait with the Monitor tool until {repo}-wt-accept/.live-run/duress-launch.log holds a line starting exit=, re-arming the Monitor each time it stops (it is capped at thirty minutes); the pack is the one {repo}-wt-accept/.live-run/latest.txt names once that line is there
runs.command: nohup bash -c 'mkdir -p {repo}-wt-accept/.live-run; LIVE_RUN_DURESS_MS=7800000 timeout 8100 {node} {repo}-wt-accept/apps/desktop/scripts/live-run.mjs --confirm --skip-build --only=duress > {repo}-wt-accept/.live-run/duress-launch.log 2>&1; echo "exit=$?" >> {repo}-wt-accept/.live-run/duress-launch.log' > /dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null & disown

runs.what: the opt-in scenarios cutoff, rename, plan-open and empty-answer (empty-answer runs empty-answer, empty-once and empty-wait)

autopsy.method: For the live-run packs (`.live-run/runs/<stamp>/`, the newest named in `.live-run/latest.txt`), follow .agents/skills/run-autopsy/SKILL.md for EVERY session; the product reader is apps/desktop/scripts/autopsy.mjs.
